metadata.description: A collection of Agent Skills for GitHub Copilot and other skills-compatible agents, grouped into installable plugins.

plugins.name: testing
plugins.description: Write, review, and debug automated tests in whatever framework a repository already uses. Detects the stack at runtime rather than imposing a framework. With your agreement, it installs the project's own test runner when it is missing, and review-tests may run the project's documented setup — never anything else, and never unattended.

plugins.name: review
plugins.description: Review code against Google's Standard of Code Review and the repository's own rules files and review checklist, reporting findings with Conventional Comments labels and CWE-named security categories. Also generates those rules files and the checklist the review reads. It also reviews the interface a change produces, from screenshots, DOM and styles, for WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility, consistency, clarity and unintended visual change.

plugins.name: docs
plugins.description: Write architecture documentation, a product manual, or a document following your own template from repository source, verified dependency and call evidence, and reviewed prose — you choose the outline, none is mandatory — and check existing docs against a template. Produces multi-page docs with file:line citations and a human checkpoint for the final readings.

plugins.name: development
plugins.description: Implement a feature, bug fix, or refactor and verify it against the original request — acceptance criteria fixed before coding, design patterns used only for a concrete problem, and evidence reported for every check. Builds from a supplied design or an approved plan, working on the plan's own branch.

plugins.name: reasoning
plugins.description: Plan a change for review and hand-off, without touching code: analyze-requirements compares a new requirement with its previous version, tracks the open points for the PO through DoU files, and splits the result into epics; design-solution answers advice and comparison questions in the conversation, write-plan saves a plan on its own branch, and coder-handoff dispatches the approved plan to a coder subagent, reviews the branch, and opens the pull request. Meant for sessions on a high-tier model.

plugins.name: verification
plugins.description: Set up a repository's own verification — its build, lint, static analysis, and test checks with pass/fail criteria, a feature map, and evidence capture — and verify any existing change against its goal, with evidence for every check and criterion and one honest verdict.

plugins.name: skill-authoring
plugins.description: Evaluate Agent Skills on three levels — static structure and scope, whether they trigger on the right requests and stay quiet on the wrong ones, and whether they lead an agent to the right outcome compared with no skill — by writing eval suites for `claude plugin eval` and reporting what each failure means.

plugins.name: presentation
plugins.description: Make or refine simple, visual PowerPoint slides: workflows, processes, before/after and operating models drawn as framed blocks of icon-and-label nodes in 2–3 colours, built on the user's own .pptx with its theme kept. Requires python-pptx and Pillow, which it never installs.
